policy_title: Amend NHS Constitution for Single-Sex Accommodation and Same-Sex Care
stated: The Conservative Party will amend the NHS Constitution to recognise every patient’s right to request single-sex accommodation and same-sex intimate care, and will ensure words like 'breastfeeding' and 'mother' are not replaced.

source.quote: We will amend the NHS Constitution so that it recognises every patient’s right to request single-sex accommodation and same-sex intimate care. We will not allow the word ‘woman’ to be erased by health services. Words such as ‘breastfeeding’ and ‘mother’ will not be replaced by ‘chestfeeding’ and ‘birthing parent’.

bearing_set.reason: Amending the NHS Constitution to codify sex-based rights to accommodation and intimate care directly engages the legal-rights framework, equal treatment and anti-discrimination protections, and competing rights claims (sex-based vs gender-identity-based) — squarely within O9's strict scope.

The right to request same-sex intimate care materially affects whether certain patients (e.g. survivors of sexual violence, those with strong religious convictions) can effectively access NHS treatment without deterrence or distress — a real verdict on care access.

The right to request same-sex intimate care is squarely a bodily autonomy protection for patients (one of O10's core indicators), and the language clause (protecting terms like 'mother' and 'breastfeeding' in NHS documents) engages with institutional speech norms in a public body — together these earn a real verdict on personal liberty and bodily autonomy.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O9 (equal treatment — contested between sex-based and gender-reassignment-based protections in NHS settings) and O10 (bodily autonomy in intimate care, plus institutional expression norms). O3 is not in scope because this policy does not materially affect the O3 indicators (waiting lists, access, capacity); it changes the conditions and rights framework within which NHS care is delivered, not whether care can be accessed.
